terms.comment: Latin has no everyday word for a fortnight and counts the days, as Livy does with intrā quīndecim diēs (37.1.6). “For a fortnight” is the accusative alone: quattuordecim diēs.
A rare word from Columella’s farming calendar, easily taken for sēmestris, “of six months”.

phrases.latin: Avia quattuordecim diēs apud nōs manēbit.
phrases.english: Grandma will stay with us for a fortnight.

sources: Lewis & Short: quattuordecim · Lewis & Short: semestrium
